nuevos.descripcion:
Metformin and berberine are both known for lowering blood sugar—but new research suggests part of the reason may be happening somewhere unexpected: your intestines.

Metformin can mildly inhibit mitochondria inside intestinal cells. With less mitochondrial activity, these cells shift toward using more glucose for energy. Instead of simply absorbing glucose and passing it into the bloodstream, the intestinal cells begin consuming more of it themselves.

Essentially, the intestine may become a metabolic sink for glucose, pulling glucose out of circulation and burning it for energy.

And there’s human evidence supporting part of this mechanism. In people with type 2 diabetes, metformin treatment approximately doubled glucose uptake by the small intestine. Importantly, the human study demonstrated increased uptake—it did not directly prove that the glucose was subsequently metabolized exactly as demonstrated in the mechanistic experiments.

Interestingly, berberine appears to use a similar intestinal mechanism. When researchers prevented mitochondrial inhibition in intestinal cells, berberine no longer produced the same glucose-lowering effect.

How to Use This: This doesn’t change whether metformin or berberine is appropriate for you, but it changes our understanding of how they may work. Their glucose-lowering effects may involve not only the liver, but also turning the intestine into a significant consumer of glucose.

outliers.descripcion:
Entrainment is one of the most powerful aspects of our biology.

Our circadian rhythm is created within us, but numerous studies show that our health is best when it is entrained to the rising and setting of the sun. That’s not to say you have to wake up at sunrise, but people who try to live nocturnally definitely suffer health consequences and people who match their sleep rhythm even somewhat to the rising and setting of the sun (one form of entrainment), derive many health benefits.

Entrainment works on shorter time scales too. Exercise at roughly the same time for a few days and you’ll notice your energy will increases a few minutes before that typical workout time.

Study or do some reading or some other form of work or learning at roughly the same time or times per day, and you’ll notice that your mental sharpness will start to increase in anticipation of those times.

To be clear, some of this is psychological, but a lot of it is physiological. The neuromodulators, hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate alertness and focus are readily susceptible to entrainment.

And entrainment is a concept that we can leverage. Not to make us rigid, but understanding it can help you make better sense of why you are more energetic and mentally sharp at particular times of day, and it can give you flexibility over what those times are.
